historycoolkids In 2015, Dr. Randal Olson, a data scientist, designed what he calls the "perfect" U.S. road trip by applying genetic algorithms, a type of search heuristic, to solve the classic Traveling Salesman Problem. 

The goal was to find the most efficient route that visits either 50 major national landmarks or all 47–50+ National Parks without unnecessary backtracking. The resulting iconic route spans over 13,699 miles and passes through all 48 contiguous states, hitting landmarks such as the Statue of Liberty, the Alamo, and Yellowstone. While the raw driving time is around 224 hours, a realistic trip with sightseeing typically takes 2 to 3 months.

СДВГ нельзя рассматривать как временную проблему, которая исчезает после школы. Баркли вводит термин «временная близорукость»: мозг человека с этим диагнозом не выстраивает рабочую связь между текущим поведением и его последствиями в будущем. Это приводит к формированию стиля жизни, который планомерно разрушает здоровье через четыре зоны риска:

1 Нарушение биологических ритмов. Из-за дефицита исполнительных функций саморегуляция сна и питания становится невозможной. Хронический недосып и импульсивное пищевое поведение ведут к ранним метаболическим нарушениям.

2 Медицинская запущенность. Пациенты с СДВГ систематически пропускают плановые обследования и не доводят лечение текущих заболеваний до конца. В результате излечимые патологии переходят в разряд смертельно опасных.

3 Рискованное поведение как поиск стимуляции. Пониженный уровень дофамина заставляет человека искать внешние стимулы через высокую скорость на дорогах или употребление психоактивных веществ.

Graham Weaver’s 30-second unstuck technique targets avoidance, the root of most paralysis in decisions or tasks. 

Ask these four questions rapidly, aloud if possible, in under 30 seconds total:

•	What am I avoiding? Pinpoint it exactly—like a hard email or job talk. Specificity unlocks momentum.

•	Why am I avoiding it? Name the fear or boredom honestly; this shrinks its grip.

•	What’s the cost? Tally lost time, stress, or opportunities to spark urgency.

•	What’s my plan now? Commit to one tiny step, like drafting a subject line.

Speed cuts overthinking. Small action dissolves resistance, per Weaver’s investor and teaching insights.

This is how authoritarian power trains people to live in a constant state of learned helplessness: a condition where any action feels impossible or pointless. You begin to feel foolish or even guilty for believing that something could be changed.

I was raised in Russia, and I battle this feeling inside myself every day. This work is one way I try to uproot it. The result is a 30-second animated horror short, “Repeat After Me.”

Timothy Snyder ( @thetimothysnyder ) warns, “Don’t obey in advance.” But when generations before you have never seen action lead to a positive outcome, what in your own life suggests that acting would make a difference?

From the outside, nothing looks obviously wrong. In authoritarian systems, life often appears normal. People go to work, have dinner, and carry on as usual. As Ernst Fraenkel wrote, “The Dual State lives by veiling its true nature.” Because nothing seems urgent, things become distorted slowly, and people learn to stay quiet and not interfere.

A pair of hippopotami scrap it out beside the dining area of Tafika camp in South Luangwa.

During the dumpening, the tail is used to fling feces as far as 10 meters (32.8ft) from the extrusion site, spraying turds as far as he can on either side in an attempt to claim this land as his own.

Anyway, leave it to me to focus on the 10 seconds of pooping and not the 87 seconds of hippo fisticuffs.
